questions.statement: I ________ to Cartagena three times. It's a beautiful city!
questions.context: Talking about having visited a place.

options.feedback: Incorrect. We use Present Perfect for experiences.
Correct! Present Perfect (have + past participle) for life experiences.
Incorrect. This is present tense.
Incorrect. "I" takes "have", not "has".

questions.explanation:
El Presente Perfecto se utiliza para hablar de experiencias que han ocurrido en algún momento de la vida, sin especificar exactamente cuándo.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: ________ you ever ________ an exotic fruit like a pitahaya?

options.feedback: Incorrect. This is for habits.
Incorrect. This is for a specific time in the past.
Correct! "Have + past participle" for questions about experiences.
Incorrect. "You" takes "have".

questions.explanation:
Para preguntar sobre experiencias de vida usamos "Have you ever + participio pasado".

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: My sister ________ already ________ her homework, so she can go out.
questions.context: Third person singular in Present Perfect.

options.feedback: Incorrect. My sister (she) takes "has".
Correct! Third person singular (he/she/it) uses "has".
Incorrect. Grammatically incorrect for present perfect.
Incorrect. "Did" is for Past Simple questions/negatives.

questions.explanation:
En el Presente Perfecto, recordamos cambiar el auxiliar a "has" cuando el sujeto es he, she o it.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Juan has lived in Medellín ________ he was a little boy.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "For" is used for periods of time (e.g., 5 years).
Correct! "Since" is used for a specific starting point in time.
Incorrect. Not the standard preposition for present perfect duration.
Incorrect. This means he stopped living there.

questions.explanation:
Usamos "since" para indicar el punto de inicio de una acción que continúa hasta el presente.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: We have studied English ________ five years.

options.feedback: Correct! "For" is used to show a duration or period of time.
Incorrect. "Since" needs a specific point in time, not a number of years.
Incorrect. "Ago" is only used with Past Simple.
Incorrect. "Yet" is used for expectations in negatives/questions.

questions.explanation:
"For" se utiliza para indicar la duración de una acción (cuánto tiempo ha pasado).

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Shakira ________ many awards throughout her career.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Her career is ongoing, so Present Perfect is better.
Correct! Present perfect connects the past with the current status of her career.
Incorrect. Shakira (she) takes "has".
Incorrect. This is present simple.

questions.explanation:
Cuando hablamos de los logros de alguien que sigue activo en su carrera, el Presente Perfecto es el tiempo más apropiado porque los eventos pueden repetirse.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: I ________ a lot of coffee today, but yesterday I ________ any.
questions.context: Contrasting Present Perfect and Past Simple.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Tenses are in the wrong places.
Correct! "Today" is an unfinished time (Present Perfect); "yesterday" is finished (Past Simple).
Incorrect. "Yesterday" requires Past Simple.
Incorrect. Grammatically incorrect forms.

questions.explanation:
Este es un punto clave de B1: usar Presente Perfecto para tiempos no terminados (today, this week) y Pasado Simple para tiempos terminados (yesterday, last year).

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
**A:** "Are you hungry?"
**B:** "No, thanks. I've ________ had a big lunch."

options.feedback: Correct! "Just" indicates that the action happened a very short time ago.
Incorrect. "Yet" goes at the end of negative sentences or questions.
Incorrect. "Ever" is for questions about experiences in general.
Incorrect. Would mean you haven't eaten, but the response says "no thanks".

questions.explanation:
La palabra "just" se coloca entre el auxiliar y el participio para indicar que una acción acaba de ocurrir.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Where is Maria? She's ________ to the supermarket. She'll be back in ten minutes.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Been" means she went and came back.
Correct! "Gone" means she is still at the destination or on her way there.
Incorrect. We need a participle after "has" ('s).
Incorrect.

questions.explanation:
En Presente Perfecto, "been" indica que el viaje se completó (fue y volvió), mientras que "gone" indica que la persona aún está allá.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Which part of this text contains a grammatical error?
"I have **known (A)** my best friend **for (B)** ten years. We **have met (C)** in primary school and we **have been (D)** inseparable since then."
questions.context: Identifying errors in a complex paragraph.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Correct participle for "know".
Incorrect. Correct preposition for a period of time.
Correct! This is an error. Meeting someone is a specific event in the past; it should be "We met" (Past Simple).
Incorrect. Correct use to show a state that continues to the present.

questions.explanation:
En B1 se debe saber que eventos únicos de inicio (como conocer a alguien o nacer) se expresan en Pasado Simple, aunque la relación resultante use Presente Perfecto.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the most natural dialogue for a mother checking her son's chores:

options.text: "Have you finished yet?" - "Yes, I already did."
options.feedback: Incorrect. Past simple is possible in American English but Present Perfect is preferred in B1 tests.

options.text: "Have you finished your chores yet?" - "Yes, I have already finished them."
options.feedback: Correct! Uses both "yet" and "already" perfectly in Present Perfect.

options.text: "Did you finish already?" - "No, I haven't finished already."
options.feedback: Incorrect. "Already" is not used in negative responses of this type; "yet" is needed.
Incorrect. Grammatically broken.

questions.explanation:
"Yet" se usa en preguntas y negativas (al final), mientras que "already" se usa en afirmaciones para indicar que algo ocurrió antes de lo esperado.

questions.statement:
"Gabriel García Márquez won the Nobel Prize in 1982. He wrote many books that have changed world literature. Even though he died in 2014, his work has remained a symbol of Latin America."
What is the best way to describe his impact?

options.text: His historical achievements in the past continue to influence the present world.
options.feedback: Correct! It summarizes the mix of Past Simple (achievements) and Present Perfect (influence).

options.text: He is going to write more books about Macondo in the future.
options.feedback: Incorrect. He is deceased.

options.text: He has never won an important award during his life.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Contradicts the text.

options.text: He only wrote books for people in Colombia.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Text says he changed "world literature".

questions.explanation: Crear una síntesis requiere entender cómo las acciones terminadas (Past Simple) de figuras históricas tienen efectos duraderos (Present Perfect) en la cultura actual.
